hypothesis: If the claim holds, sunflower spiral families will intersect at a constant, generally non-right angle, with right-angle intersections rare.
pass_criterion: In at least 30 measured sunflower capitula, fewer than 20% of measured spiral crossings are within 5 degrees of 90 degrees, and the crossing angle is constant within a capitulum (SD < 5 degrees).
fail_criterion: More than 50% of crossings are within 5 degrees of 90 degrees, or the angle varies by more than 15 degrees across the disc.
interpretation: 'Isogonal' means constant crossing angle, and 'orthogonal' means 90 degrees. The test is of measured parastichy crossing angles in the capitulum.
no_dataset_reason: I know of no public dataset, verified by me, that records measured parastichy crossing angles in sunflower capitula. Available data are mostly parastichy counts, which cannot decide the claim.
